```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Prepare one survey design

Declare the cohort in `nis_design()` and keep the columns needed by the
summary and model.

```{r design}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50") |>
  dplyr::mutate(death = as.integer(DIED))
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = AGE >= 18,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED, death, heart_failure),
  annualize = TRUE
)
```

The design contains adult cohort rows. For hospital-years with no cohort rows,
`nis_design()` adds placeholder rows so those hospital-years remain represented
in the design's variance structure. This placeholder method is experimental;
review the design construction and its suitability for your analysis.

## Estimate weighted summaries

`srvyr` adds tidy verbs to survey designs. The total below is an annualized
weighted discharge estimate; the mean and its standard error use the survey
design.

```{r srvyr}
srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_age = srvyr::survey_mean(AGE),
  death_rate = srvyr::survey_mean(death)
)
```

All values come from invented rows and illustrate output shape only.

## Build a Table 1

`gtsummary::tbl_svysummary()` formats weighted descriptive statistics. These
optional packages are needed for this section.

```{r table, eval=rlang::is_installed(c("gtsummary", "cardx", "survey", "gt"))}
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = heart_failure,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, LOS, DIED)
) |>
  gtsummary::add_overall()
table_one
```

The columns compare the flag groups with an overall column. Inspect the
unweighted cell counts before sharing; the table is not automatically
disclosure-cleared.

## Fit a survey-weighted model

`survey::svyglm()` fits generalized linear models using the design.

```{r model, eval=rlang::is_installed("survey")}
fit <- survey::svyglm(
  death ~ heart_failure + AGE + FEMALE + factor(YEAR),
  design = design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)
summary(fit)
```

Coefficients describe model associations under the survey design; they do not
establish causality. The synthetic data are too small and artificial for
substantive conclusions.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Use `survey`/`srvyr` methods on the survey design, not ordinary row-level
>   summaries when reporting design-based uncertainty.
> - A weighted estimate does not validate the cohort definition, model, or
>   causal interpretation.
> - Apply disclosure review separately; weighted summaries alone do not show
>   whether counts are safe to report.

See [Survey design and weighting](survey-design.html),
[`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html), and
[Disclosure and suppression](disclosure.html).
